title: Stochastic Thermodynamics of Score Matching in Diffusion Models
authors: Xuehao Ding, H. T. Quan, Yuhai Tu
abstract: Score-based diffusion models are a powerful class of generative AI systems capable of sampling from complex, high-dimensional probability distributions. Their dynamics consist of a forward diffusion process that transforms data into noise and a learned reverse process that reconstructs data by reversing the probability flow. Here, we develop a stochastic thermodynamic framework for diffusion models and their score-matching objective. We introduce a trajectory-dependent quantity, time-asymmetry entropy production (TAEP), defined from the forward and reverse diffusion dynamics, and show that it obeys exact fluctuation theorems. Remarkably, Hyvärinen's implicit score-matching kernel emerges naturally as a fluctuating component of TAEP, while the average TAEP is exactly proportional to the score-matching objective. We further show that fluctuations of TAEP quantify sampling unevenness and provide a thermodynamic measure of data-manifold coverage. These results yield a quantitative explanation for the superior sampling diversity of diffusion models and reveal a thermodynamic mechanism by which stochastic gradient descent favors flatter, more generalizable solutions. By uncovering the entropic nature of score matching, our work establishes fundamental statistical-mechanical principles underlying diffusion-based generative AI.
summary: This work establishes a stochastic thermodynamic framework for diffusion models by introducing the Time-asymmetry Entropy Production (TAEP). It proves that the average TAEP is proportional to the score-matching objective and obeys fluctuation theorems. This offers a deep, physical understanding of why these generative models achieve high sampling diversity.
main_problem: To develop a stochastic thermodynamic framework for score-based diffusion models, relating their training objective to fundamental principles like entropy production.
main_result: The average Time-asymmetry Entropy Production (TAEP) is exactly proportional to the score-matching objective, and TAEP obeys exact fluctuation theorems. This provides a thermodynamic explanation for the superior sampling diversity of diffusion models.
method: The authors introduce TAEP, a trajectory-dependent quantity derived from forward and reverse Langevin dynamics, and apply concepts from non-equilibrium statistical physics, including fluctuation theorems.
model_or_system: The system is score-based diffusion models, which model data generation via a forward diffusion process (data to noise) and a learned reverse sampling process. The analysis treats these processes as stochastic physical systems.
key_observables: Time-asymmetry Entropy Production (TAEP), its fluctuations ($	ext{Var}(\Delta s_{	ext{ta}})$), and the ensemble average $\langle \Delta s_{	ext{ta}} angle$.
important_parameters: The proportionality constant relating $\langle \Delta s_{	ext{ta}} angle$ to the score-matching objective, and the noise strength/curvature of the loss landscape.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on interpreting diffusion models as stochastic physical systems and assumes sufficient network expressivity for the reverse process to approximate the true score function.
figures_summary: Figures show TAEP distributions verifying fluctuation theorems, tracking data manifold coverage via $	ext{Var}(\Delta s_{	ext{ta}})$ during training, and demonstrating a positive correlation between SGD noise covariance and the loss landscape Hessian.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the stochastic framework (Langevin equations) to deriving TAEP, proving it obeys fluctuation theorems, establishing its proportionality to the score-matching objective, and finally analyzing how fluctuations quantify sampling unevenness and guide optimization towards flatter minima.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous physical interpretation of modern generative AI objectives using established tools from non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, linking machine learning loss functions directly to thermodynamic quantities like entropy production.
